Cheng Yi's view on the Pu case does not apply: Renzong raised Yingzong and had no son, and Prince Pu had other sons. Xiaozong's line is continued through Wuzong and you; making you Xiaozong's son abandons your father and leaves Wuzong without a successor. When famine struck Yansui, Xia Yan recommended Left Censor-in-Chief Li Rugui as grand coordinator.
When famine struck Yansui, Xia Yan recommended Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Rugui as grand coordinator.
僉都御史 is an assistant censor-in-chief, not the left censor-in-chief (左都御史).
Yansui was famine-stricken; Yan recommended Left Censor-in-Chief Li Rugui as grand coordinator.
Yansui was famine-stricken; Yan recommended Assistant Censor-in-Chief Li Rugui as grand coordinator.
僉都御史 is an assistant censor-in-chief, not the left censor-in-chief (左都御史).

Fujing deeply resented Xia Yan's standing with the emperor; Yan in turn resented Fujing's sudden appointment of Peng Ze as Grand Master of Ceremonies without supporting him—and friction opened between them.

Fujing deeply resented Xia Yan's standing with the emperor; Yan in turn resented Fujing's sudden appointment of Peng Ze as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices without supporting him—and friction opened between them.
太常卿 is the chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
Fujing then greatly resented Yan's favor; Yan also resented Fujing suddenly employing Peng Ze as Grand Master of Ceremonies without supporting him—the two thus had a rift.
Fujing then greatly resented Yan's favor; Yan also resented Fujing suddenly employing Peng Ze as Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices without supporting him—the two thus had a rift.
太常卿 is the chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
In the third month of the tenth year (1531) he was promoted to Junior Tutor and concurrent Hanlin Academician, placed in charge of the Hanlin Academy while continuing his lectures as before.

In the third month of the tenth year (1531) he was promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Hanlin Academician, placed in charge of the Hanlin Academy while continuing his lectures as before.
少詹事 is the Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Junior Tutor.
In the third month of the tenth year he was promoted to Junior Tutor, concurrently Hanlin Academician, directing the academy affairs, daily lectures as before.

In the third month of the tenth year he was promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Hanlin Academician, directing the academy affairs, daily lectures as before.
少詹事 is the Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Junior Tutor.
When the emperor visited Mount Dayu, Xia Yan was slow in submitting the edict appointing a regent during the imperial absence, and the emperor rebuked him sharply.
When the emperor visited Mount Dayu, Xia Yan was slow in submitting the edict for those left to guard the capital during the imperial absence, and the emperor rebuked him sharply.
居守敕 is the edict for officials left guarding the capital, not the appointment of a regent.
The emperor visited Dayu Mountain; Yan's submitted residence-guard edict was slightly late; the emperor rebuked and reproached him.
The emperor visited Dayu Mountain; Yan's submitted edict for guarding the capital was slightly late; the emperor rebuked and reproached him.
居守敕 is the edict for officials left guarding the capital.
The emperor's wrath did not ease; suspecting Xia Yan of having defamed him, he ordered the Ministry of Rites to reclaim the items.
The emperor's wrath did not ease; suspecting that Xia Yan had damaged or destroyed them, he ordered the Ministry of Rites to reclaim the items.
毀損 here means damaging the bestowed seal and edicts, not defamation.
The emperor's anger did not subside; suspected Yan of slander and damage, and ordered the Ministry of Rites to pursue recovery.
The emperor's anger did not subside; suspected Yan of having damaged them, and ordered the Ministry of Rites to pursue recovery.
毀損 here means damaging the bestowed seal and edicts, not slander.
Xia Yan was stripped of his Junior Preceptor title and noble rank, and retired as Junior Guardian, Minister, and Grand Secretary.
Xia Yan was stripped of his Junior Preceptor title and his merit and prestige ranks, and retired as Junior Guardian, Minister, and Grand Secretary.
勛階 are merit (勛) and prestige (階) ranks such as Superior Pillar of State and Specially Advanced Grand Master, not a noble rank.
Stripped Junior Preceptor noble rank; as Junior Guardian, Minister, and Grand Secretary he retired.
Stripped of Junior Preceptor and his merit and prestige ranks; as Junior Guardian, Minister, and Grand Secretary he retired.
勛階 are merit and prestige ranks, not a noble rank.
After a few days the emperor's anger cooled and he ordered the punitive measures stopped.
After a few days the emperor's anger cooled and he ordered him to halt his departure.
命止行 means he was ordered to stop leaving (for retirement), not that punitive measures were halted.
After several days the anger subsided; ordered the punitive measures halted.
After several days the anger subsided; ordered him to halt his departure.
命止行 means he was ordered to stop leaving (for retirement).
Before long, lightning struck the Hall of Imperial Supplication.
Before long, lightning struck the Fengtian Hall (Hall of Revering Heaven).
奉天殿 is the Fengtian Hall, the main audience hall; 'Imperial Supplication' misrenders 奉天.
Before long, thunder struck the Hall of Imperial Supplication.
Before long, thunder struck the Fengtian Hall (Hall of Revering Heaven).
奉天殿 is the Fengtian Hall, the main audience hall; 'Imperial Supplication' misrenders 奉天.
When Shaanxi reported a military victory, Xia Yan was restored as Junior Preceptor and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Minister of Personnel, and given a post at the Huagai Hall.

When Shaanxi reported a military victory, Xia Yan was restored as Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Minister of Personnel, and made Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.
太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent (太子太傅 is the Mentor title used elsewhere); 華蓋殿 here abbreviates 華蓋殿大學士, Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall.
Shaanxi reported victory; restored Junior Preceptor and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Minister of Personnel, Huagai Hall.
Shaanxi reported victory; restored Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Minister of Personnel, Huagai Hall.
太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; 太子太傅 is the Mentor title used elsewhere.
Previously, Yan composed blue liturgies and other writings most suited to the emperor's intent.
Previously, Yan composed qingci (Daoist prayers written on blue paper) and other writings most suited to the emperor's intent.
青詞 are Daoist prayers written on blue paper (qingci), not 'blue liturgies'.
Guo Xun's defense was insolent and defiant; the emperor was enraged and stripped his ally Wang Tingxiang of his official standing.
Guo Xun's defense was insolent and defiant; the emperor was enraged and stripped Guo Xun's colleague Wang Tingxiang of his official standing.
勛同事 means Guo Xun's colleague (co-administrator), not his ally.

Guo Xun was thrown into prison; Xia Yan was restored as Junior Mentor, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, resuming duty once his illness had cleared.

Guo Xun was thrown into prison; Xia Yan was restored as Junior Mentor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall, resuming duty once his illness had cleared.
太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
Thereupon Xun was imprisoned; Yan was restored as Junior Mentor, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Wuying Hall Grand Secretary, entering duty when his illness recovered.
Thereupon Xun was imprisoned; Yan was restored as Junior Mentor, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Wuying Hall Grand Secretary, entering duty when his illness recovered.
太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
Yan Song was Xia Yan's fellow townsman; calling himself Xia Yan's senior, he had served him with elaborate deference.
Yan Song was Xia Yan's fellow townsman; honoring Xia Yan as the one who had risen first, he had served him with elaborate deference.
稱先達 here means Yan Song honored Xia Yan as his senior in career success, consistent with serving him deferentially.
Song and Yan were from the same native place; calling himself a senior, he served Yan very carefully.
Song and Yan were from the same native place; hailing Yan as his senior in success, he served Yan very carefully.
稱先達 here means Yan Song honored Xia Yan as his senior in career success.
When Xia Yan entered the Grand Secretariat he had brought Yan Song in as his protégé and treated him like a household retainer—an indignity Yan Song deeply resented.
When Xia Yan entered the Grand Secretariat he recommended Yan Song to succeed him and treated him like a household retainer—an indignity Yan Song deeply resented.
援嵩自代 means he recommended Yan Song as his own replacement (as Minister of Rites).
More than ten days later, on the taboo day of Emperor Xian of Han, Xia Yan was still summoned to pay respects and wait on duty in the Western Park.
More than ten days later, on the death anniversary of Emperor Xian (Shizong's father, the Xingxian Emperor), Xia Yan was still summoned to pay respects and wait on duty in the Western Park.
獻帝 here is Shizong's father, the Xingxian Emperor, not Emperor Xian of Han; 諱辰 is a death anniversary.
After more than ten days, on Emperor Xian's taboo day, Yan was still summoned to enter and pay respects and await duty at the Western Park.
After more than ten days, on Emperor Xian's death anniversary, Yan was still summoned to enter and pay respects and await duty at the Western Park.
諱辰 is the death anniversary of Shizong's father, the Xingxian Emperor.
Censor Qiao You, Supervising Secretary Shen Liangcai, and others submitted memorials discussing Xia Yan's case and asked to be punished themselves for speaking out.
Censor Qiao You, Supervising Secretary Shen Liangcai, and others submitted memorials discussing Xia Yan's case and also asked to be punished themselves.
且請罪 says only that they also asked for punishment; 'for speaking out' is not in the text.

The exile of Bureau Director Gao Jian, the dismissals of Tang Long, Xu Chengmou, Cui Tong, Wang Yongbin, and Huang Zuo, and the imprisonments of Wang Gao, Wang Wei, and Sun Jilu—all were Xia Yan's doing.

The exile of Bureau Director Gao Jian, the dismissals of Tang Long, Xu Chengming, Cui Tong, Wang Yongbin, and Huang Zuo, and the imprisonments of Wang Gao, Wang Wei, and Sun Jilu—all were Xia Yan's doing.
許成名 is read Xu Chengming (名 ming).
Bureau of Appointments Director Gao Jian exiled to garrison; Tang Long, Xu Chengmou, Cui Tong, Wang Yongbin, and Huang Zuo dismissed; Wang Gao, Wang Wei, and Sun Jilu imprisoned—all Yan directed.
Bureau of Appointments Director Gao Jian exiled to garrison; Tang Long, Xu Chengming, Cui Tong, Wang Yongbin, and Huang Zuo dismissed; Wang Gao, Wang Wei, and Sun Jilu imprisoned—all Yan directed.
許成名 is read Xu Chengming (名 ming).

Finally, when Censor Chen Qixue impeached Cui Yuan and Brocade Guard Commander Lu Bing on a salt-monopoly matter, Xia Yan drafted a rescript ordering Chen to formalize his charges—charges that were fabricated and called for death sentences; Lu Bing had to kneel for a long time before the matter was dropped.

Finally, when Censor Chen Qixue impeached Cui Yuan and Brocade Guard Commander Lu Bing on a salt-monopoly matter, Xia Yan drafted a rescript ordering the two accused to explain themselves; both went to Xia Yan to beg for mercy, and only after Lu Bing knelt for a long time was the matter dropped.
令陳狀 orders the accused to explain themselves; 皆造言請死 means both went to (造) Xia Yan (言) to beg for mercy, not 'fabricated charges'.

Finally Censor Chen Qixue on a salt law matter impeached Cui Yuan and Brocade Guard Commander-in-Chief Lu Bing; Yan drafted a rescript ordering Chen to submit his statement; all fabricated charges begging death; Bing long kneeled before obtaining release.

Finally Censor Chen Qixue on a salt law matter impeached Cui Yuan and Brocade Guard Commander-in-Chief Lu Bing; Yan drafted a rescript ordering them to submit statements; both went to Yan begging for their lives; Bing long kneeled before obtaining release.
皆造言請死: both went to Xia Yan begging for their lives.
When Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian of Shaanxi memorialized for recovering the Ordos, Xia Yan endorsed the proposal.
When Supreme Commander Zeng Xian of Shaanxi memorialized for recovering the Ordos, Xia Yan endorsed the proposal.
總督 is a supreme commander (governor-general), not a grand coordinator (巡撫).
Because Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian requested recovery of the Ordos, he approved and decided it.
Because Shaanxi Supreme Commander Zeng Xian requested recovery of the Ordos, he approved and decided it.
總督 is a supreme commander (governor-general), not a grand coordinator (巡撫).

Yan Song then had Qiu Luan draft a memorial accusing Xia Yan of taking bribes from Zeng Xian and trading favors for profit. The case implicated Su Gang, and Zeng Xian and Su Gang were clapped into the imperial prison.

Yan Song then drafted a memorial in Qiu Luan's name accusing Xia Yan of taking bribes from Zeng Xian and trading favors for profit. The case implicated Su Gang, and Zeng Xian and Su Gang were clapped into the imperial prison.
代仇鸞草奏 means Yan Song drafted the memorial on Qiu Luan's behalf.

Song again had Qiu Luan draft a memorial denouncing Yan for receiving Xian's gold and colluding for corrupt profit; the matter implicated Su Gang; thus Xian and Gang were sent to the imperial prison by edict.

Song again drafted a memorial on Qiu Luan's behalf denouncing Yan for receiving Xian's gold and colluding for corrupt profit; the matter implicated Su Gang; thus Xian and Gang were sent to the imperial prison by edict.
代仇鸞草奏 means Yan Song drafted the memorial on Qiu Luan's behalf.
When the case was finalized, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao and others sentenced Yan to death, citing the provisions on officials of merit and talent above.

When the case was finalized, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao and others sentenced Yan to death, citing the provisions for deliberating on the noble and the able, and submitted it to the throne.
援議貴議能條以上: they cited the 議貴/議能 leniency provisions and submitted (以上) the case; 'above' misreads 以上.

His wife, Lady Su, was banished to Guangxi. His nephew Ke Cheng, a department director, and his grand-nephew Chao Qing, an assistant in the Court of Imperial Studs, were struck from the rolls and reduced to common status.

His wife, Lady Su, was banished to Guangxi. His nephew Ke Cheng, a ministry secretary, and his grand-nephew Chao Qing, an assistant in the Seal Office, were struck from the rolls and reduced to common status.
主事 is a ministry secretary, not a department director; 尚寶丞 is an assistant of the Seal Office (尚寶司), not the Court of Imperial Studs (太僕寺).
His wife the Su was exiled to Guangxi; his nephew, Department Director Ke Cheng, and grand-nephew, Court of Imperial Studs Assistant Chao Qing, were struck from the registry and made commoners.
His wife the Su was exiled to Guangxi; his nephew, Ministry Secretary Ke Cheng, and grand-nephew, Seal Office Assistant Chao Qing, were struck from the registry and made commoners.
主事 is a ministry secretary; 尚寶丞 is an assistant of the Seal Office.
When Yan died, the wife brought her back; his appearance very much resembled Yan.
When Yan died, the wife brought him back; his appearance very much resembled Yan.
逆之歸 refers to bringing back the son, not the concubine.
Yet ambition and arrogance filled his memoirs, and in the end Yan Song forced him out.
Yet he grew proud in will and overbearing in spirit, and in the end Yan Song forced him out.
誌驕氣溢 (誌 = 志) describes his proud will and overflowing spirit; there are no memoirs.
Yet his will records pride overflowing; in the end he was squeezed out by Song.
Yet his will was proud and his spirit overflowing; in the end he was squeezed out by Song.
誌驕氣溢: proud in will, overflowing in spirit.

unresolvedReferences.description: 石缶 (Shi Fu) is transcribed as in the text; it may be a corrupted form of another official's name. Not resolved here.
太后 (the empress dowager) is not identified in this chunk; kept as a title-only person.
The text writes 孕敬, evidently a graphic error for 孚敬 (Zhang Cong's granted name); linked to Zhang Cong.
黃綰 is romanized Huang Wan here but Huang Guan in chunk 001; same characters, so the same person.
範純仁 is the common variant writing of 范純仁 (Fan Chunren).
慈壽太后 (Empress Dowager Cishou) is identified with Empress Zhang, later styled Zhaosheng (昭聖), as in chunk 003.

彭澤 here is a senior minister who had left court (listed with Lin Jun and Sun Jiao), distinct from the Personnel department director Peng Ze, Zhang Cong's ally, in chunks 002-003; kept as a separate person.
The empress dowager whose temple-visit rites were debated is inferred to be Shizong's mother (Empress Dowager Xingguo), since the Shi Temple honored her husband.
石缶 may be a corrupted writing of Shi Bao 石珤; kept as written.
天子 in s0243-s0244 is a generic maxim ('none but the Son of Heaven'), not a direct reference; disposed as a title.
彭澤 implicated in the Chen Jiuchou case is taken to be the senior minister Peng Ze (as in s0264), distinct from the Personnel department director Peng Ze of chunks 002-003.
桂林 is read as the name of an usher (Gui Lin), referred to as 林 in s0327; the translation treats it as 'Guilin' and is repaired.
陳九疇 is romanized 'Chen Jiuchi' in the translation; the standard reading is Chen Jiuchou.
太王 and 王季 appear only in Chinese; the idiomatic translation renders them as 'his forebears'.
範純仁 is a variant writing of 范純仁 (Fan Chunren).
黃綰 is romanized 'Huang Guan' here (as in chunk 001) but 'Huang Wan' in chunk 003; same person.
彭澤 here is Zhang Cong's ally (the former Personnel department director of chunks 002-003) promoted to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, distinct from the senior minister Peng Ze of chunks 004b/005.
汪鋐 is mis-romanized 'Wang Qian' in the translation; repaired to Wang Hong.
The text writes 陳後, a conversion error for 陳后 (Empress Chen); 陳后 is Shizong's first empress (Empress Chen); the translation's 'deposed' and 'execute' misread 殺…喪 (diminishing her mourning rites).
張糸采 is a split rendering of 張綵 (Zhang Cai), the Zhengde-era minister.
莊奉夫人 and 肅奉夫人 are court-lady titles; their surnames (Xing, Gu) are inferred from their brothers' names.
後 (the empress) in 後親蠶北郊 is Shizong's reigning empress, not named in the passage; kept as an unnamed person rather than identified.
The prince (皇子) born before the intercalary twelfth month of Jiajing 15 is not named in the passage; he is kept as an unnamed son of Shizong rather than identified.
The intercalary twelfth month of Jiajing 15 falls around the turn of 1536/1537; dates are given as the 1536-1537 bound.
慈慶 and 慈寧 (the two palaces whose dowagers died) are linked to Empress Dowager Zhaosheng and to Shizong's mother by palace residence; the text does not name either.
The heir apparent (太子) is not named in this passage; kept as an unnamed son of Shizong.
獻帝 is Shizong's father (Xingxian Emperor); the draft translation had wrongly identified him as Emperor Xian of Han.
Lady Su (妻蘇) is taken to be the successor wife (繼妻) whose father was Su Gang (s0709) and the jealous wife of s0744-s0745; the identification rests on the surname and context.
從子 Kecheng and 從孫 Chaoqing entail unnamed brothers of Xia Yan and Chaoqing's father; whether Chaoqing descends from Kecheng is not stated, so separate unnamed intermediaries were kept.
The concubine and her son are unnamed; the son's paternity by Xia Yan is inferred from 妾有身 and his resemblance to Xia Yan.
